_comment: Catalog of derived Trisul counter groups (crosskey, filter, keyset). Live inventory always wins: call list_all_available_counter_groups before proposing create_*. Never copy GUIDs from this file.
reuse_first: Always call list_all_available_counter_groups (and get_cginfo_from_countergroup_name for candidate names) before proposing or creating. If a live group already matches the dimensions, filter rules, or keyset buckets, reuse its GUID. Only create when nothing suitable exists, via confirm=False then explicit user confirmation then confirm=True.

how_to_choose.if_user_wants: A relationship or drill-down between two (or three) dimensions: interface-to-app, host-to-country, A-by-B, sankey, tree
The same keys as a parent group, but only traffic that matches (or excludes) specific keys from another group: HTTPS-only hosts, DNS on interfaces
Several parent keys rolled into named buckets that appear as new toppers: web vs dns vs p2p, server farms, office vs DC interfaces

show_in_module_overview.crosskey: Must use template 109 (tree) or 110 (sankey) when the user asked for A-by-B / tree / sankey. The created GUID goes in options.cgguid. Composite keys can also drive ordinary toppers/charts (3, 102) if the user asked for a list or pie of the crosskey itself.
show_in_module_overview.filter: The new group behaves like the parent: keys are still parent keys (hosts, interfaces, …), just restricted. Put its GUID in cgguid (templates 1, 3, 56, 61, 109 if parent is already a crosskey) or in models[].cgguid (54, 101, 102, 103) or counter_group (105).
show_in_module_overview.keyset: The new group's keys ARE the bucket names (web, p2p, gateways). Chart or list those bucket names. Template 3/56 for a bucket toppers table, 102 pie of buckets, 101/54/61/105 for a named bucket.

types.name: Crosskey counter group
types.what_it_is: A derived counter group whose keys are pairs (or triples) of keys from two or three parent groups. Each composite key records traffic that belongs to both dimensions at once, e.g. this-host AND that-app.
types.how_it_works: Trisul crosses every key of cross_guid1 with matching keys of cross_guid2 (and optionally cross_guid3). Typical names look like Hosts_X_Apps or FlowIntf_bx_Apps. Slice keys are enabled so dashboards can expand a parent into children.
types.use_when: The metric is a relationship between dimensions: who talks to whom, which apps on which interface, host-to-country, sankey ribbons, expandable A-by-B tree.
types.not_when: Do not use for a session flowmap (template 107, no counter group). Do not create a crosskey just to fill a theme-dashboard sankey slot if a live _X_ / _bx_ group already exists. Do not use when the user only wants a subset of one group's keys (that is filter) or named buckets of keys (that is keyset).
how_to_create: Call list_all_available_counter_groups. Reuse any live group that already crosses the same dimensions (names with _X_, _bx_, or ' x ').
Resolve parent names to GUIDs with get_cginfo_from_countergroup_name. Never ask the user for GUIDs.
Call create_crosskey_counter_group with confirm=False, creation_reason (inventory was checked, nothing fits), and dashboard_usage (template id and which option gets the new GUID).
If status is reuse_existing, use an existing_counter_groups GUID and stop.
If status is pending_confirmation, show type, name, both parent names/GUIDs, reason, and the exact module that will consume the GUID. Ask for confirmation.
After explicit approval, call again with the same arguments and confirm=True. Use the returned counter_group_guid in the dashboard module.

types.name: Filtered counter group
types.what_it_is: A derived group that keeps the parent's key space (hosts, interfaces, …) but only meters traffic that matches include keys — or drops traffic matching inverse keys — taken from a second counter group (the filter group).
types.how_it_works: Parent supplies what you display. Filter group supplies which keys qualify the traffic. Include list (filter_key_list) AND/OR exclude list (filter_key_inv_list). Keys are stored in Trisul DB format (p-0035 for DNS, p-0050,p-01BB for 80+443). Human labels such as dns are resolved via search_keys inside the create tool.
types.use_when: The user wants toppers or charts of a familiar parent, restricted to a protocol, app, country, or other qualifier: HTTPS-only hosts, DNS on interfaces, hosts talking to India, everything except web on an interface.
types.not_when: Do not use when they want an A-by-B relationship (crosskey) or named aggregate buckets that replace the original keys (keyset). Do not use a filter when an existing native group already is that subset (e.g. HTTP Hosts).
how_to_create: Call list_all_available_counter_groups. Reuse an existing filter with the same parent, filter group, and include/exclude keys.
Resolve parent and filter group names to GUIDs with get_cginfo_from_countergroup_name.
Pass explicit keys (Port-80, p-0035, 53, full IP, ranges a~b) or labels (dns, http). The tool resolves labels.
Call create_filter_counter_group with confirm=False plus creation_reason and dashboard_usage.
If status is reuse_existing, use that GUID.
If keys are ambiguous, show candidates and ask the user to pick — do not guess.
Show the proposal (parent, filter, resolved DB keys, module usage) and wait for confirmation, then confirm=True.

types.name: Keyset counter group
types.what_it_is: A derived group that folds many keys from one parent into named buckets. Each KeysetKey (web, p2p, gateways) becomes a first-class key whose meters are the sum of its KeyFrom members.
types.how_it_works: Parent is the source key space. Each bucket is {keyset_key, keys_from}. KeysetKey must not contain comma, tilde, or !. KeyFrom is stored in DB format, comma-separated, ranges allowed (p-1AE1~p-1AE9). meter_only_keysets=true (default) counts only keys that belong to a bucket. You may create an empty group (name + parent) and add buckets later.
types.use_when: The user wants custom aggregates that do not exist as native keys: business vs recreational apps, server farms, office vs datacenter interfaces, P2P as one number.
types.not_when: Do not use to restrict toppers to a few keys while still showing those original keys (that is a filter, or key_filter on a module). Do not use for A-by-B drill-down (crosskey).
how_to_create: Call list_all_available_counter_groups. Reuse a keyset with the same parent and bucket purpose/name.
Resolve the parent GUID with get_cginfo_from_countergroup_name.
Supply one bucket (keyset_key + keys_from) or several via keysets=[{keyset_key, keys_from}, ...]. Labels in keys_from are resolved against the parent.
Call create_keyset_counter_group with confirm=False, creation_reason, dashboard_usage.
If reuse_existing, use that GUID. If keys are ambiguous, ask the user to pick.
Show every KeysetKey and resolved KeyFrom plus the module that will chart the buckets, then confirm=True.
